title: The guard does not read a sed script as a path
why: A guard reads the script argument of a sed command as a file path, so a harmless edit is judged as a write to a path it names (coordinator, 02:47 CST Nov 8; lane test-dirs-include-testing, 03:22 CST Nov 8).
note: Fix: the guard skips a sed script argument (the first non-option word, or each -e value) when it collects paths, and still reads each file operand. Red case first: a sed command whose script text looks like a path is refused or asked today; control: a sed -i on a guarded file still refuses.
